source_text: Omnta ergo recapitulans recapitulatus est, et adversus inimicum nostrum bellum provocans, et elidens eum qui, in initio in Adam captivos duxerat nos, et caleans ejus caput, quemadmodum habes in Genesi dixisse serpenti Deum: Et inimicitiam ponam inter te et inter mulierem, et inter semen tuum et semen ejus: tpse tuum lobservabit caput, et tu observabis ejus calcanewm, Ex eo enim qui ex muliere Virgine habebat nasci secundum similitudinem Adam, preeconabatur observans caput serpentis, id est semen, de quo ait Apostolus in epistola que est ad Galatas: Legem + factorum s positam, donec veniret semen cui promissum est. Manifestius autem adhue in eadem ostendit epistola, sic dicens: Cum autem venit plenitudo temporis, misit Deus Filium suum, factum de muliere. Neque enim juste victus fuisset inimicus, nisi ex muliere homo esset, qui vicit eum. Per mulierem enim homini dominatus est ab initio, semetipsum contrarium statuens homini. Propter hoc et Dominus semetipsum Filium Hominis confitetur, principalem hominem illum, ex quo ea que secundum mulierem est plasmatio facta est, in semetipsum recapitulans: uti quemadmodum per hominem victum descendit in mortem genus nostrum, sic iterum per victorem ascendamus in vitam. Et quemadmodum accepit palmam mors per hominem adversus nos, sic iterum nos adversus mortem per hominem accipiamus palmam. 2. Non autem Dominus antiquam illam et primam adversus serpentem inimicitiam in semetipso recapitulatus fuisset, adimplens promissionem Demiurgi, et perficiens preeceptum ejus, si ab alio venisset patre. Sed quoniam unus et idem est, qui ab initio plasmavit nos, et in fine Filium suum misit, preeceptum ejus perfecit Dominus, factus ex muliere, et destruens adversarium nostrum, et perficiens hominem secundum imaginem et similitudinem Et propter hoc non aliunde eum destruxit, nisi ex dictionibus Legis, et Patris preecepto adjutore usus ad destructionem et traductionem apostate angeli. Primo quidem diebus xu. jejunans, similiter ut Moyses et Helias, postea esuriit, ut hominem verum et firmum intelligamus: proprium enim est hominis, jejunantem esurire: deinde autem, ut haberet adversarius ubi congrederetur. Quoniam enim in principio per escam, non esurientem hominem seduxit transgredi preeceptum Dei, in fine esurientem non potuit dissuadere, eam que a Deo esset, sustinere escam. enim eo, et dicente: Si jilius Dei es, dic ut lapides isti panes fant; Dominus autem per preeceptum Legis repulit eum, dicens: Scriptum est, Non in pane tantum vivit homo. Ad illud quidem quod ait, Si filius Dei es, tacuit: exceecayit autem eum hominis confessione, et per paternam dictionem primum ejus impetum evacuavit. Que ergo fuit in Paradiso repletio hominis per duplicem gustationem, dissoluta est per eam, que fuit in hoe mundo, indigentiam. Ille autem legaliter explosus, tentabat et ipse per mandatum rursus legitime facere congressionem. In altissimum enim templi pinnaculum ducens eum, dixit: Si jilius Dei es, mitte te deorsum. Scriptum est enim: Quoniam Angelis swis Deus mandavit de te, et in manibus tollent te, ne forte offendas ad lapidem pedem twum, mendacium abscondens per Scripturam, quod Illud enim, quod Angelis suis mandavit de eo, scriptum erat; Mitte te autem deorsum, * de eo nulla dicebat sed a semetipso hane suasionem Diabolus afferebat. Dominus itaque legitime confutavit eum, dicens: Item seriptum in Lege ostendens id Yuidem quod est secundum hominem, quoniam non debet homo tentare Deum; quantum autem ad illum, in eo homine qui videbatur, non tentaret Dominum Deum suum. Elatio itaque sensus que fuit in serpente, dissoluta est per eam que fuit in homine humilitas: et bis jam victus erat de Scriptura Diabolus, cum est traductus, contraria preecepto Dei suadens, et secundum sententiam suam Dei hostis ostensus. Qui magne confutatus, et quasi semetipsum colligens, universam quam habebat virtutem in mendacium ordinans, tertio ostendit e seculi regna omnia, et gloriam ipsorum, dicens, quemadmodum meminit Lucas: Hee omnia tibi dabo, quoniam mihi tradita sunt, et cui volo do ea, si procidens adoraveris me. Dominus itaque eum qui esset: Vade, inquit, Satana; seriptum est Senim: Dominum Deum tuum adorabis, et illi soli servies. Denudans eum per hoe nomen, et se ostendens qui erat. Satana enim verbum Hebraicum, Apostatam significat. Et tertio itaque vincens eum, in reliquum repulit a semetipso quasi legitime vicet soluta est ea que fuerat in Adam preecepti Dei preevaricatio, per preeceptum legis, quod servavit Filius hominis non transgrediens preeceptum Dei. 8. Quis ergo Dominus Deus, cui Christus testimonium perhibet; quem nemo tentabit, et quem omnes adorare oportet, et soli servire? Omnimodo ille est sine dubio, qui et Legem dedit Deus. Heee enim in Lege preedicta fuerant, et per Legis sententiam ostendit Dominus, quoniam Lex quidem a Patre Verbum Domini annuntiat : apostata autem Dei angelus )per illius destruitur vocem, traductus Nquis esset, et victus a Filio hominis servante Dei preeceptum. Quoniam enim in initio homini suasit transgredi preceptum factoris, ideo eum habuit in sua potestate; potestas autem ejus est transgressio et apostasia, et his colligavit hominem ; per hominem ipsum iterum oportebat victum eum contrario colligari iisdem vinculis, quibus alligavit hominem, ut homo solutus revertatur ad suum Dominum, illa vincula relinquens, per }quze ipse fuerat alligatus, id est transgressionem. Illius enim colligatio, solutio facta est hominis, quoniam non potest ali> quis introire in domum fortis, et vasa ejus diripere, nisi primum ipsum fortem alligaverit. Contraria ergo in sermone ejus, qui omnia fecit Dei, traducens eum Dominus, et subjiciens per preeceptum, preeceptum autem Dei, lex; fugitivum eum Homo ejus et legis transgressorem, et apostatam Dei ostendens, postea jam ®Verbum constanter eum colligavit, quasi suum fugitivum, et diripuit ejus vasa, id est, eos qui ab eo detinebantur homines, quibus ipse injuste utebatur. Et captivus quidem ductus est juste is qui hominem injuste captivum duxerat; qui autem ante captivus ductus fuerat homo, extractus est a possessoris potestate, secundum misericordiam Dei Patris: qui miseratus est plasmati suo, et dedit salutem ei, per Verbum, id est per Christum redintegrans: ut experimento discat homo, quoniam non a semetipso, sed donatione Dei accipit incorruptelam. Dominus verus, et Deus unus a lege declaratur, et Evangelio per Christum ejus Filium manifestatur : quem solum adorare, et ab illo omnia bona exspectare oportet, non a Satana.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore recapitulating all things, He recapitulated, and provoking war against our enemy, and striking him who had led us captive from the beginning in Adam, and bruising his head, just as God said to the serpent in Genesis: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed: he will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel. For from the one who was to be born from the Virgin, according to the likeness of Adam, it was foretold that he would bruise the serpent's head, that is, the seed, about which the Apostle says in the epistle to the Galatians: The law of works was established until the seed to whom the promise was made should come. But more clearly, the same epistle shows, saying: When the fullness of time came, God sent His Son, made from a woman. For the enemy would not have been justly conquered if a man from a woman had not conquered him. For through a woman, the enemy dominated man from the beginning, setting himself contrary to man. On account of this, the Lord also confesses Himself to be the Son of Man, the first man, from whom the creation that is according to the woman was made, recapitulating it in Himself: so that just as our race descended into death through the conquered man, so we may ascend into life through the conqueror. And just as death received a palm against us through man, so we will receive a palm against death through man. The Lord would not have recapitulated in Himself the ancient and first enmity against the serpent, fulfilling the promise of the Creator and perfecting His command, if He had come from another father. But since He is one and the same who from the beginning created us and in the end sent His Son, the Lord perfected His command, made from a woman, and destroyed our adversary, and perfected man according to the image and likeness. And on account of this, He did not destroy him from anywhere else, except from the words of the Law and the command of the Father, using them as a helper for the destruction and translation of the apostate angel. First, indeed, on the fortieth day, fasting, similarly to Moses and Elijah, afterwards He was hungry, so that we may understand Him to be a true and firm man: for it is proper to man to be hungry when fasting: then, however, so that the adversary might have something to attack. For since in the beginning he deceived man, who was not hungry, to transgress the command of God through food, in the end he could not persuade the hungry man to sustain the food that was from God. For when he said: If you are the Son of God, say that these stones become bread, the Lord repelled him through the command of the Law, saying: It is written, Man does not live by bread alone. To what he said, If you are the Son of God, He was silent: but He confounded him by the confession of man and through the paternal word, He first emptied his attack. What, therefore, was the fullness of man in Paradise through the double tasting, was dissolved through the hunger that was in this world. But he, having been legally refuted, tried to make an attack again through a command. For leading Him to the highest pinnacle of the temple, he said: If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down. For it is written: For God has commanded His angels concerning you, and they will lift you up in their hands, lest you strike your foot against a stone, hiding the lie through Scripture, that what was written concerning His angels, He commanded concerning Him: Throw yourself down, however, he did not say anything about Him, but the Devil was bringing this persuasion from himself. Therefore, the Lord legally confounded him, saying: It is also written in the Law, showing what is according to man, that man ought not to tempt God: as for Him, however, in the man who seemed to be, He did not tempt the Lord His God. The elevation of sense, therefore, which was in the serpent, was dissolved through the humility that was in man: and the Devil was already twice conquered from Scripture, when he was translated, persuading what was contrary to the command of God, and showing himself to be the enemy of God. Who, having been greatly confounded, and as if gathering himself, ordering all his power into a lie, showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, saying, as Luke remembers: I will give all these things to you, because they have been handed over to me, and I give them to whomever I want, if you, falling down, worship me. Therefore, the Lord said to him: Go, Satan; for it is written: You will worship the Lord your God, and serve Him only. Uncovering him through this name, and showing Himself to be who He was. For Satan is a Hebrew word, signifying Apostate. And thus, conquering him a third time, He repelled him from Himself, as if legally: the transgression of God's command, which was in Adam, was solved through the command of the Law, which the Son of Man kept, not transgressing the command of God. Who, therefore, is the Lord God, to whom Christ bears witness; whom no one will tempt, and whom all ought to adore, and serve only? Without a doubt, He is the one who gave the Law, God. For these things were predicted in the Law, and the Lord shows through the sentence of the Law, that the Law indeed announces the Word of the Lord from the Father: but the apostate angel of God is destroyed through His voice, translated, and conquered by the Son of Man, keeping the command of God. For since in the beginning he persuaded man to transgress the command of the Creator, therefore he had him in his power; but his power is transgression and apostasy, and through these he bound man: through man, however, it was necessary that he be conquered again, bound by the same chains by which he bound man, so that man, having been freed, may return to his Lord, leaving behind the chains by which he was bound, that is, transgression. For the binding of him was the liberation of man, since no one can enter the house of the strong man and plunder his vessels, unless he first binds the strong man. Therefore, the Lord, translating him through the contrary in His word, and subjecting him through the command, and the command of God being the Law, showed him to be a fugitive from God and a transgressor of the Law, and an apostate of God: afterwards, indeed, the Word firmly bound him, as if he were His fugitive, and plundered his vessels, that is, the men who were detained by him, whom he was using unjustly. And the one who had led man captive unjustly was justly led captive: but the man who had been led captive before was extracted from the power of the possessor, according to the mercy of God the Father: who pitied His creation and gave salvation to him through the Word, that is, through Christ, restoring him: so that man may learn by experience that he receives incorruptibility not from himself, but from the gift of God. The true Lord, and the one God, is declared by the Law, and is manifested through the Gospel by His Son Christ: whom alone we ought to adore, and from whom we ought to expect all good things, not from Satan.

pass_b_english: In the beginning, God said to the serpent in Genesis (Genesis 3:15), 'I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed: he will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.' This prophecy was fulfilled when the Lord, born of a woman, bruised the serpent's head, which represents the seed of evil. The Apostle Paul explains in his epistle to the Galatians (Galatians 3:19) that the law was established until the seed to whom the promise was made should come. When the fullness of time arrived, God sent His Son, made from a woman, to conquer the enemy and perfect humanity according to God's image and likeness.

The Lord's victory over the enemy was just, for it was a man born of a woman who conquered him. Through a woman, the enemy had dominated humanity from the beginning, setting himself contrary to humanity. The Lord, as the Son of Man, recapitulated humanity in Himself, so that just as our race descended into death through the conquered man, we may ascend into life through the conqueror. The Lord's hunger, after fasting for forty days like Moses and Elijah, showed that He was a true and firm man, for it is human to be hungry when fasting.

The Devil tried to deceive the Lord, saying, 'If you are the Son of God, say that these stones become bread.' But the Lord repelled him, saying, 'It is written, Man does not live by bread alone' (Deuteronomy 6:13). The Devil then tried to persuade the Lord to throw Himself down from the pinnacle of the temple, quoting Scripture out of context. However, the Lord confounded him, saying, 'It is also written, You shall not tempt the Lord your God.' The Devil's power is transgression and apostasy, and through these, he bound humanity. But the Lord, through His obedience to God's command, conquered the Devil and freed humanity from his power.

The Lord's victory over the Devil was complete when He said, 'Go, Satan; for it is written, You will worship the Lord your God, and serve Him only' (Deuteronomy 6:13). The Devil, whose name means 'Apostate' in Hebrew, was uncovered and repelled by the Lord. The Lord, as the Son of Man, kept God's command and did not transgress, solving the transgression of God's command that was in Adam. The true Lord God, who gave the Law, is declared by the Law and manifested through the Gospel by His Son Christ, whom alone we ought to adore and from whom we ought to expect all good things, not from Satan. The Lord's mercy and salvation are available to all humanity through His Son Christ, and we ought to learn by experience that we receive incorruptibility not from ourselves, but from the gift of God.

The Lord's word and the Law of God are the same, and through them, the Devil is destroyed and humanity is freed. The Lord, as the Word of God, firmly bound the Devil and plundered his vessels, freeing humanity from his power. The one who had led humanity captive unjustly was justly led captive, and humanity was extracted from the power of the possessor, according to the mercy of God the Father. Through the Word, that is, through Christ, God pitied His creation and gave salvation to humanity, restoring them to their rightful place. The Lord, and the one God, is declared by the Law, and is manifested through the Gospel by His Son Christ, whom alone we ought to adore, and from whom we ought to expect all good things, not from Satan, as Luke remembers the Devil's words, 'I will give all these things to you, because they have been handed over to me, and I give them to whomever I want, if you, falling down, worship me' (Luke 4:5-7).

review.notes: Pass B is a summary/paraphrase rather than a translation, failing the completeness requirement. It omits significant portions of the text's theological argumentation, specifically the detailed discussion regarding the 'double tasting' (repletio/indigentiam) in Paradise versus the world, the specific mechanics of how the Lord 'emptied' the attack through the 'confession of man' (exceecayit autem eum hominis confessione), and the extensive concluding section regarding the 'strong man' (fortis) and the 'vessels' (vasa) which is presented in Pass B across multiple disjointed paragraphs rather than following the source structure. Furthermore, Pass B introduces interpretations not present in the Latin, such as 'the seed of evil' for 'semen' and 'quoting Scripture out of context' for the Devil's temptation, which violates the rule that B must neither add to nor contradict A or the Greek. It also fails to maintain the single-paragraph structure of the source, instead splitting the content into five distinct paragraphs.
